newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped 2.39 points on Sunday in quiet trade in which many popular stocks closed unchanged or slightly down, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed at 378.41 from Thursday's 380.8 in average trade of 68.74 million pounds ($20.25 million).
"The market was generally down today. Trading is low and people are scared to buy at these prices. We might see a turnaround soon though," said Ehab el-Mahallawi at Intercapital brokerage.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development led the day's top ten most active stocks, with trade worth more than 26.00 million pounds but it closed 0.25 points lower at 491.

The stock has been suffering from an announcement that shareholders will have to wait to qualify for their one-for-one free share. The original cut-off date was March 31 but the company postponed it indefinitely because of a technical hitch.

The company said it would announce a new date as soon as the stock exchange agreed to register the capital increase. Without this the new shares would have had to trade over-the-counter in parallel with the old ones.
Mahallawi said the cement sector generated good volume on Sunday.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was the day's second most active share and led the popular sector. Tora shares worth more than 6.60 million pounds changed hands but it slipped 0.49 to close at 97.

The cement firm announced on Sunday that its net after-tax profits rose to 78.5 million pounds ($23 million) in the first half of the 1996/7 financial year from 63.45 million in the same period of the previous year.

Helwan Portland Cement closed 0.4 pounds higher at 78 after shares worth more than 2.60 million pounds were traded. Suez Cement ended trading 1.00 pounds lower at 70 after shares worth more than 2.40 million pounds changed hands.

North Cairo Flour Mills ended trading unchanged at 190 with shares worth more than 3.70 million pound being traded. Southern Cairo Flour Mills rose 0.25 pounds to 80.90 while the other milling shares ended lower.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 575.3 points from 585.62 points on Thursday. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 264.46 from 264.32.
Out of the 75 shares traded on Sunday, 24 gained, 32 lost and 19 ended unchanged.
